notes: Account summary: Ironwood Cortex is building a unified legal research platform for enterprise law firms + corporate legal departments.
They plan a single global index (sharded) with projected 200M-800M embeddings in year 1; long-term target 1B+.
Primary workflow: candidate retrieval via ANN -> fast cross-encoder reranker for reordering (precision critical for legal citations).
Latency targets: <=100ms end-to-end for retrieval+rerank on single-query hot-path; 95p goal 150ms. Throughput: peak 120 qps for search cluster.
Cost targets: aim for <$0.003 per query (embeddings + ANN + rerank amortized) using batching, quantization, and dedicated capacity.
Model preferences: open LLMs for re-ranker (cross-encoder), FP16 / quantized embedder (int8/4) for vector generation; willing to test Redwood-verified variants.
Operational needs: predictable autoscaling, granular per-route cost telemetry, token-level cost breakdown for reranker models.
Data constraints: PII redaction in embeddings pipeline, data residency in NA, strict retention policies (7 years archival), audit logging required for search events.
POC notes: ran 50M vector pilot on dedicated instances. Observed KV cache hit-rate 24% with current workload; requesting caching recommendations from Optimize team.
Customer quoted: 'Precision trumps raw recall for our use cases — a bad rerank is worse than a slightly smaller recall set.'
Internal: SE recommended hybrid routing: low-latency replicas for live search, cold infill through lower-cost batches for long-tail queries.
